summary: SL-088 made the reveal land or refuse. It deleted ShellReveal.Walk's nearest-ancestor climb and RevealKind.Ancestor, and added a Failed kind, a status line and a resolve-back guard. It also added an R-002 window case, U-114-safe landing comparison and an architecture rule against Explorer's select switch. The product delta was small. Most of the cost went into the tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 harness and one parse edge the design assumed away, over 3 builds, 5 code reviews and 6 validates. The slice was accepted without the live window run: criteria 1, 2 and 5 and the 1 s bound were never observed on any SL-088 build, and Hidden+System targets still report success.

payload.reason: Reflection over the full record. Validate #6 accepted build attempt 3 (c26d3fe) without the live Explorer window run.

payload.estimate_error: Opened as medium, low risk, one designer. The risk tier was too low and the size was right for src only. The low tier switched off critique and critique-review (both 'recorded no account', filed []). The problems that later cost two send-backs were critique territory: the assumption that the parse HRESULT alone means the right item, tab-shared HWNDs in the harness, and the belief that a narrower Quit() rule would let validate run the window cases unattended. The src change was a deletion plus a Failed kind, but the real work sat in the ~4,700-line WindowCases.ps1 and in Plan/Walk name handling. Actual rework: build-check 2, spike 2, design 2, build 3, code-review 5, validate 6. Critique and critique-review look perfect on this slice only because they did not run.

learned.lesson: Window cases that open real Explorer windows and drive Shell.Application (R-001, R-002 in tests/window/WindowCases.ps1) cannot be run by the loop. Any criterion whose only check is such a case will halt every validate at the same wall. Before design, mark those criteria 'person-run', or agree a run window, so validate does not loop on them.
learned.evidence: Build-check, validate #1, #3 and #5 all declined to run R-001/R-002 as 'operating another program's windows unattended'. Validate #5 wrote 'no rebuild can close it'. Validate #6 accepted without the run. The design claimed that narrowing Quit() to non-baseline windows under the fixture root removed the obstacle, and it did not.

learned.lesson: Do not tier a slice low when it changes the Windows shell integration (ShellReveal.cs, Plan/Walk parse handling) or WindowCases.ps1. The low tier is what skips critique and critique-review, and the flaws found later were exactly what a critique asks.
learned.evidence: Critique #1 and critique-review #1 were skipped as a sizing decision. Afterwards code review and validate found m1 (tab-shared HWNDs), R2-m2 (false reserved-name refusal), m3, m4 and the unattended-run assumption, costing 2 send-backs.

learned.lesson: SHParseDisplayName returning S_OK does not prove it parsed the target. A trailing-dot name like 'dup.' parses to 'dup', and bare device names misparse. Paths of 301+ characters come back as 8.3 aliases. So Exact must mean the parsed ID list resolves back to the requested path (GetLongPathName compare) and the open returned S_OK. Reserved-name refusal must compare the whole component with trailing spaces trimmed, because con.txt, aux.h, nul.log and com1.txt are addressed exactly on Windows 11.
learned.evidence: Build 1's IsMisparsed used the text before the first dot and refused con.txt with a false reason, pinned by an InlineData in the Plan unit test. The mis-parse was found by code review and confirmed against the real shell by validate #2. Build 2 fixed it and added the resolve-back check and ParsedAsAnotherItem, which the design never mentioned. Windows 10 parse behaviour for these names is unmeasured.

learned.lesson: On the reveal feature, size by the proof harness, not by src. ShellReveal's mechanism was already correct from SL-047 and the product change was a deletion. Every later cycle was spent in WindowCases.ps1 (Check-Landing, Close-CaseWindows, Compare-ExplorerState, Get-ExplorerHwndCounts).
learned.evidence: Build-check: 'most of the reveal mechanism already exists'. The spikes landed 36/36, 12/12 and 12/12 on the existing TryReveal. The diff for build attempt 3 was one ShellReveal.cs comment plus WindowCases.ps1. Attempt 3 was a full build/review/validate cycle for two minor harness findings.

learned.lesson: Each fix to WindowCases.ps1 gets reviewed again and tends to produce a new finding: m4 was created by the fix for m1, and m3 sat unnoticed through three review rounds. For the next harness edit, have the reviewer read the whole touched function set in the first pass and fix the harness findings before validate runs.
learned.evidence: m1 was fixed in build 2. That fix introduced m4 (unreadable entries invisible to the Quit guard). m3 ([void](Check-Landing ...)) dated from build 1 and surfaced only in code-review #4. Both drove validate #4's send-back.

learned.lesson: The harness logic in WindowCases.ps1 can be tested without opening Explorer by loading functions from the script's AST and running them against a fake Shell.Application (a New-Object stub whose entries record Quit()), in both pwsh 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1. The builder and the validator each wrote this as a throwaway. Keep it as a repo test the next time WindowCases.ps1 changes.
learned.evidence: Build #3 and validate #5 each loaded Check-Landing, Get-ExplorerHwndCounts and Close-CaseWindows from the AST into a fake and then deleted the temp harness. That is the only evidence that Close-CaseWindows never quits a shared-HWND tab, and it was verified only for a single-entry desktop.

learned.lesson: The select-switch rule is dual-written as '(?mi)/select\b' over all of src/**/*.cs, comments included, ShellReveal.cs not exempt, above the '# settled by' marker with including_comments: true. No comment or string anywhere in src may spell the switch; write 'Explorer's select switch'. Adding a rule still needs eng/rules-parity.ps1 to AGREE in both shells (15 facts, 39 patterns at this slice).
learned.evidence: Build #3 checked with a separate Select-String that the new Walk comment did not trip the rule. The SL-047 rule '/select\s*,' missed ArgumentList.Add("/select"), "/SELECT," and "/select \"".

learned.lesson: A spike that needs a person to change the machine (here HKCU Explorer\Advanced Hidden=2) halts the loop, but the loop proceeds anyway ('built anyway despite a go spike') and the finding is carried as an unowned unmet criterion. Anything left out of scope for that reason needs its own backlog item at design time.
learned.evidence: Spike reveal-selects-hidden-and-system-items finished with H+S 0/8 selected and H-only 5/5 under Hidden=1, with the Hidden=2 run pending. Validate #6 still lists 'criterion not met: 14. Hidden+System target'.

missed.what: The design claimed that narrowing the Quit() close rule to non-baseline windows under the fixture root removes the build check's reason for not running R-001 unattended, so criterion 5 could be validated. The objection was never only Quit() reach. R-001 and R-002 open real Explorer windows on the person's desktop and drive another program through Shell.Application. A check would ask what exactly stopped the last stage from running the case, and whether the design's change removes it.
missed.caught_by: validate-slice #1, #3 and #5 (halted at the same person-only gap), then accepted without the run at #6

missed.what: Key decision 'no File.Exists; the SHParseDisplayName HRESULT is the only existence test' assumed S_OK means the target item. Nobody asked what an S_OK parse resolves to. 'dup.' parses to 'dup' and bare device names misparse, so the reveal could land on another item, which criterion 6 forbids. The build added an unplanned Plan-level name refusal, then in attempt 2 an unplanned resolve-back check (ParsedAsAnotherItem).
missed.caught_by: the build's own declared deviation and code-review, then build attempt 2's resolve-back check

missed.what: IsMisparsed took the reserved-name base from the text before the first dot. It refused con.txt, aux.h, nul.log and com1.txt with a false reason ('reserved device name') though the shell addresses them exactly on Windows 11. The unit test pinned the wrong answer with InlineData C:\con.txt. Nothing had measured how the shell parses those names before a refusal was shipped.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 2 (R2-m2), confirmed on the real shell by validate-slice #2, which sent the slice back

missed.what: The design's window-matching and cleanup keyed on the baseline HWND and compared only $old[0]. On Windows 11 the tabs of one Explorer window are separate Shell.Application entries sharing an HWND. The critique should have asked what Shell.Application reports for a tabbed window. With 2+ tabs open, R-002 step (e) and R-001 step 3 report a false 'window moved' failure, and a case tab opened inside a baseline window is never closed.

All four R-002 landing steps called [void](Check-Landing ...) from build attempt 1, which discards every ok/FAIL line and the 'landed N ms after the click' figure. The run prints only 'FAILED: R-002' or 'PASSED', so a miss of the 1 s bound would come back without step, check or milliseconds. Three code-review rounds passed it.

Build attempt 2's fix for m1 computed 'other windows on this HWND' from Get-ExplorerWindows, which silently drops entries whose Document is null or whose read throws. A case tab sharing an HWND with one of the person's unreadable tabs would be Quit(), and Quit() on a tab entry was never measured. The previous review round accepted the fix without asking what the filter drops.

what_went_wrong: Critique and critique-review were skipped on a 'low risk, minimal project' sizing, and both recorded no account. The design's assumptions were then tested by code review and validation instead. Result: 3 builds, 5 code reviews, 6 validates, and two send-backs.

Validate halted at the same person-only wall three times (#1, #3, #5) and failed twice (#2, #4). #6 accepted without the live run. Criteria 1, 2 and 5, the deny-all landing, the 161/300/1000-character landings, the ≤1000 ms cold first reveal and the existing SC-007 cases were never observed on any SL-088 build. Acceptance rests on the refusal step (e) through the shipped exe, a real-shell Walk probe, and SL-047-era spikes that re-implemented the sequence in pwsh.

Build 1 shipped a real product defect: a name-based refusal that rejected con.txt, aux.h, nul.log and com1.txt with a false message. A unit test pinned the wrong answer. Build 2 fixed it and added an unplanned resolve-back check and failure reason that the design and design note never described.
The third build/review/validate cycle was harness-only (m3, m4, both minor). Its product diff was one comment. m4 was created by the fix for m1, and m3 had been present since build 1.

The Hidden+System spike never finished because it needs a person to change Explorer's Hidden setting. The loop moved on. The app still reports Exact from hr==0 for targets Explorer does not select (0/8 under Hidden=1), and validate carries it as unmet with no owner.

Drift findings were repeated across two review rounds and never fixed. docs/design/SL-088-reveal-lands-or-refuses.md:45 still says Exact comes from 'S_OK alone', while Walk now also requires the resolve-back. The RevealFailure comment at MainWindow.xaml.cs:820 still covers 2 of 4 branches.

Design #1 halted on an unanswered question about criterion 4 (whether the app itself must confirm the landing). Design #2 passed on the designer's default reading. The design-level questions (R-002 vs growing R-001, status wording and others) were settled by the designer, not by a person.

Harness gaps remain. Close-CaseWindows neither quits nor reports a case tab whose Document is unreadable for the whole 5 s. Quit() on a single tab entry is unmeasured. A leftover Explorer window (HWND 723330) sits on a spike's temp tree in the person's session.
unknowns: Does the cold first reveal through the shipped exe land within 1000 ms of the click? The spikes' slowest landing was 934 ms (pwsh re-implementation, not the exe), and R-002 step (b) is the first check that times it from the hook's revealStartQpc.
Does Quit() on one tab's Shell.Application entry close only that tab or the whole Explorer window? Until measured, Close-CaseWindows can only report, not close, a case tab inside a mixed window.

Under Windows' default Explorer settings (Hidden=2), do Hidden+System targets (System Volume Information, pagefile.sys) get selected? Under Hidden=1 it was 0 of 8. The prepared run is waiting on a person.
On Windows 10, does SHParseDisplayName resolve names like con.txt to the file, or to something else that the resolve-back check must catch? Every check in this slice ran on Windows 11 26200.

Does the actual Explorer landing hold on D: (no 8.3 names) through the shipped exe and R-002 steps? Only the parse and Walk up to the open were exercised there, at 41f82cc. The spikes covered it via pwsh.

candidates.title: Run R-002 (steps a–d) and R-001 on a desktop and record the results
candidates.why: Criteria 1, 2 and 5 and the ≤1000 ms cold first reveal are still 'partial' and were never observed on any SL-088 build. The loop cannot run these cases because they open and close real Explorer windows. A person runs `pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case R-002` and `-Case R-001` after `eng/dotnet.ps1 publish`. First close the pre-existing Explorer window on the spike temp tree (HWND 723330), and keep other Explorer windows out of the way. A failure now names its step, check and landing ms.

candidates.title: Hidden+System reveal: the app says it showed the item while Explorer selects nothing
candidates.why: The spike measured 0 of 8 Hidden+System targets selected, against 5 of 5 Hidden-only, under this PC's Hidden=1, ShowSuperHidden=0. Walk reports Exact from S_OK plus the resolve-back, and the design left the H+S case unmet. System Volume Information and pagefile.sys are the typical unreadable items from the epic's failed-folders list. It first needs the Hidden=2 spike run and the person's answer on whether the app itself must confirm the landing (criterion 4's open question), so the loop should not build it unasked.

candidates.title: Correct the stale SL-088 design note and RevealFailure comment
candidates.why: docs/design/SL-088-reveal-lands-or-refuses.md:45 still says 'Exact still comes from the shell's S_OK alone', but Walk now also needs the resolve-back to match, and ParsedAsAnotherItem exists. The RevealFailure comment at MainWindow.xaml.cs:820 lists only 2 of its 4 branches. Code review flagged both in two rounds and neither blocks a pass. The next reveal slice will read the note as its authority.
